ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, point K is on the right side edge of the circle; the ray from point K upward through point L is tangent to the circle, and another line starting from K passing through the inside of the circle and extending to point J at the lower left is a chord/secant. The measure of the intercepted arc JK marked in the figure is 194°. Reasoning: What is required is ∠K, that is, the angle formed by tangent line KL and chord KJ at a point K on the circle. According to the tangent-chord theorem, the measure of the angle formed by a tangent and a chord equals half the measure of its intercepted arc. Therefore m∠K = 194° ÷ 2 = 97°.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify K as the point on the circle where a tangent ray KL touches the circle, and identify KJ as a chord/secant through the circle. The angle requested, ∠K, is the angle formed by the tangent KL and the chord KJ. Read the marked arc measure as 194° for the intercepted arc between J and K. Apply the tangent-chord theorem: the measure of an angle formed by a tangent and a chord with vertex on the circle equals half the measure of its intercepted arc. Compute m∠K = 194° ÷ 2 = 97°.
